outcomes.claim: Amnesty International identified fragments of US-made JDAM kits, with codes it associated with Boeing, at two strikes in Deir al-Balah: the al-Najjar home (10 Oct 2023, 24 killed) and the Abu Mu'eileq home (22 Oct 2023, 19 killed). It reported 43 civilians killed in total (19 children, 14 women, 10 men) and said it found no indication of military objectives at either site. Amnesty dated the recovered kits to 2017 (al-Najjar) and 2018 (Abu Mu'eileq) and estimated the bombs at about 2,000 lb and at least 1,000 lb.

outcomes.counterpoint: Amnesty sent questions to the IDF spokesperson unit on 21 Nov 2023 and reported no response by publication.
outcomes.source_note: Amnesty International is an advocacy organization; its US section publicly urged senators to support S.J.Res. 32 and S.J.Res. 138 in April 2026 (Amnesty International USA, 14 Apr 2026).
outcomes.grade_note: The grade covers Amnesty's forensic identification of the weapon. That those killed were civilians, and that there was no military objective, is Amnesty's assessment.

outcomes.claim: OCHA reports, citing the Gaza Ministry of Health (part of the Hamas-led administration in Gaza), 74,564 reported Palestinian fatalities as of 28 Oct 2026. Of these, MoH had fully identified 74,237 as of 7 Oct 2026: 35,555 men, 21,976 children, 11,301 women and 5,405 elderly.

outcomes.counterpoint: On reliability, in both directions. Higher: a capture-recapture study in The Lancet estimated 64,260 traumatic-injury deaths to 30 Jun 2024, suggesting the Ministry under-reported by 41%; peer-reviewed correspondence (2023, on the war's early counts) found the Ministry's past counts within 1.5–3.8% of UN analyses. Lower: the IDF said it had killed at least 22,000 combatants before the October 2025 ceasefire (Times of Israel, 29 Jan 2026; not independently verified); a Henry Jackson Society paper (not peer-reviewed) argues the lists include some natural deaths and that about 6,000 names were removed. The Ministry's figures do not distinguish combatants from civilians. On the composition of the dead, OHCHR verified 8,119 deaths from the first seven months, nearly 70% of them women and children; this is a verified subset (8,119 of more than 34,500 then reported), not a total, and in 88% of the verified cases five or more people were killed in the same attack. Israel rejected the report as based on 'unverified information' (Al Jazeera, 8 Nov 2024). On 30 Jan 2026 the IDF said media reports of it accepting a toll near 70,000 'do not reflect official IDF data' (Ynet, 31 Jan 2026).

outcomes.claim: On 21 Nov 2024 ICC Pre-Trial Chamber I unanimously rejected Israel's jurisdiction challenges ('Thus Israel's challenge is premature'). It issued warrants for Netanyahu and Gallant for 'the war crime of starvation as a method of warfare; and the crimes against humanity of murder, persecution, and other inhumane acts', covering 'from at least 8 October 2023 until at least 20 May 2024'. It found reasonable grounds that they 'intentionally and knowingly deprived the civilian population in Gaza of objects indispensable to their survival, including food, water, and medicine and medical supplies, as well as fuel and electricity'.

outcomes.counterpoint: The same Chamber 'could not determine that all elements of the crime against humanity of extermination were met'. Warrants are not convictions. Israel 'utterly rejects the false and absurd charges' (Prime Minister's Office, 21 Nov 2024) and contests the Court's jurisdiction. As of January 2026 two Israeli motions against the warrants remained pending; the Pre-Trial Chamber had rejected a request to suspend them on 17 Oct 2025, and the warrants 'remain in force'. On 15 Dec 2025 the Appeals Chamber, by 3 to 2, upheld the rejection of Israel's admissibility challenge (Just Security). The United States rejects the warrants: Executive Order 14203 (6 Feb 2025) imposed sanctions on the Court, calling them 'baseless arrest warrants'.
